author: WPB4
summary: Alpha.1-era research audit (CNA 7a64362e, 2026-08-11) of ContentManager, the XNB container, type readers, CNJ and content robustness, with a per-reader table and a critique of CNA's own content documents. The content deep dives already carry nearly all current substance, and many audited facts changed by 009d40f5 (Game registers readers, 61 readers, LZ4 decoded, no weak texture cache, ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder, EnumTypeReader, all surface formats). Residue added: the in-tree proof of custom XNB readers and of fresh-manager registration.

concepts.text: Content loading is one CMake module, cna_content under modules/content; it compiles the vendored cgltf single-header parser and stb image code into the same library (one CGLTF_IMPLEMENTATION translation unit, stb compiled STATIC) and adds a Draco decoder for KHR_draco_mesh_compression when that option is on.
concepts.note: Draco is no longer an optional find_package only: at 009d40f5 it is a vendored third_party/draco gitlink behind CNA_ENABLE_DRACO (ON by default, OFF for the web).

concepts.text: The content code separates namespaces by role: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Content for the XNA-faithful public API, CNA::Internal::Xnb for the binary XNB reader stack, CNA::Internal and CNA::Internal::GltfImport for the CNJ envelope, JSON and glTF import; CNB codecs and the pipeline engine live in CNA::Content::Cnb and CNA::Content::Pipeline.
concepts.note: The CNB and pipeline namespaces did not exist at the audited revision.

concepts.text: The XNB VideoReader was compiled out without FFmpeg, which made the built-in reader set platform-dependent.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 VideoReader is registered in every build; only DecimalReader is conditional (native 128-bit integer).

concepts.text: None of ContentManager's three constructors rejects a null IServiceProvider (XNA throws ArgumentNullException), and the GraphicsDevice arrives through a separate setGraphicsDevice setter; the audit also found the provider stored but never consulted.
tokens: none of the three constructors rejects a null provider
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 the provider is consulted as a fallback when no device was set; null providers remain accepted, and CNA's own tests construct standalone managers with nullptr.

concepts.text: The ContentManager member-initialiser list was written in the opposite order from the member declarations, a -Wreorder style smell with no behavioural effect.
concepts.note: Compiler-warning trivia of the audited revision with no behavioural consequence; not documentation material.

concepts.text: RootDirectory is a plain string property defaulting to "Content" and is a base, not a sandbox: BuildAssetPath joins root and name without guarding absolute names, and an explicit absolute outside-root asset is an established contract of Load.
tokens: RootDirectory is a base path, not a sandbox
an absolute name replaces the root

concepts.text: NormalizeKey folds backslashes to slashes and lowercases the name, matching FNA's OrdinalIgnoreCase asset cache.

The generic cache key is (requested C++ type, normalised name), not the name alone; a name-only key once made a second Load<T2> of the same name throw std::bad_any_cast instead of ContentLoadException, pinned by CnjAssetCacheTypeSafetyTests.

The audit counted three caches (a strong std::any cache, a weak Texture2D renderer cache, and no cache for SoundEffect and TextureCube) and three explicit Load<T> specialisations each re-implementing the XNB-first check.
tokens: There is no separate weak texture cache at this snapshot
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 there is one strong cache, TextureCube is copyable and cached, and SoundEffect is the only explicit specialisation.

concepts.text: Generic Load<T> checks disposal, the cache, then existence-ordered candidates; ResolveAssetPath tests exists() rather than has_extension() so a dotted name such as Flag.en-US still gets reader extensions, and an existing .xnb wins over .cnj and native files without fallback on a decode failure.
concepts.note: TARGET inserts the .cnb and literal-.cnb tiers after .xnb.

concepts.text: LoadXnbAsset reads the whole file, parses the 10-byte header and cross-checks the declared totalLength against the real file size before using offsets, the fix for a confirmed heap-buffer-overflow in the LZX branch.
tokens: requires 14 bytes before a compressed payload

concepts.text: XnbReadLimits::maxFileSize (64 MiB) bounds only the compressed payload before decompression; the initial whole-file read of LoadXnbAsset and the manifest scan is not capped by it.
tokens: an uncompressed .xnb between 64 MiB and 2 GiB is not refused by the file-size limit at run time
concepts.note: Verified defect CNA-BUG-017 (Known Issues).

concepts.text: Unload clears the cache without disposing any cached asset (FNA disposes tracked IDisposables first); ContentReader's manager-side disposal fallback was deferred, so no tracking list exists.
concepts.note: Issue history recorded as WP03-i003.

concepts.text: Nothing in the content path is synchronised: ContentTypeReaderManager's process-wide map has no mutex and the manager's caches are plain maps, so concurrent Load on one manager or AddTypeCreator during any Load is a data race.
The audit found that Game never called RegisterAllBuiltInXnbReaders, so a game that did not call it could not load any .xnb.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 Game's constructor registers the built-ins; a standalone ContentManager (tools, tests, C API) still needs the explicit call.

concepts.text: Game owns its ContentManager by value and setContentProperty copies the assigned manager into it, so assigning a standalone manager replaces the game's cache, readers and device pointer wholesale.
tokens: replaces the game's device pointer with null

concepts.text: The CNAEXT content manifest (RefreshContentManifest, GetContentManifest, GetXnbReaderUsageSummary) scans the root recursively, is unsorted, swallows malformed files, reports no reader names for compressed XNBs and is never consulted by Load.
ResourceContentManager was a stub whose OpenStream threw and which ContentManager never called.
tokens: OpenStream is not on the Load<T> path
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 ResourceContentManager is implemented (resource-family OpenStream); the base Load<T> still does not route through OpenStream.

concepts.text: CNJ is plain JSON with no magic bytes, header or binary layer; it was renamed from .cnb because that name implied a binary format.
tokens: no magic bytes, no fixed binary schema and no checksum
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 the .cnb extension names CNA's real binary compiled format (CNB), unrelated to CNJ.

concepts.text: ParseCnjEnvelope never throws and records a parse failure as detail; cnjVersion is kept both as integer and raw double so 1.5 is refused rather than truncated, and validation is a separate step.

The cnjVersion ceiling is per type: only Model raises it to 2 (bones array, per-mesh parentBone) and a raised ceiling does not leak to other types; the type field is a cross-check against the requested T, not the dispatch key, except for game-registered loaders.

Built-in readers accept a closed set of CNJ type values, and the sourceFile rule is enforced in code: delegating types (Texture2D, TextureCube, SoundEffect) require it, self-contained types reject it, pinned by CnjCapabilityMatrixTests.

ResolveCnjSourceFileSafely rejects empty and absolute sourceFile values, escapes found by component-wise comparison after weakly_canonical, a target that is itself .cnj and one that would resolve to a sibling .cnj.
CNJ readers were split between the recursive-descent parser CNA::Internal::ParseJson and hand-rolled substring scanners (SpriteFont, Model, SkinnedModel, colour key, custom-GLSL Effect).
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 most readers use the shared CnjCanonicalRead functions; only the custom-GLSL Effect, Model and .skinnedmodel.json still use scanners.

concepts.text: The CNJ JSON parser recurses without a depth limit, while the XNB side bounds both type-name and object nesting; a crafted deeply nested document is a stack-exhaustion vector and no CNJ fuzz test exists.
concepts.note: Verified defect CNA-BUG-016 (Known Issues).

concepts.text: RegisterCnjLoader<T>(typeName, factory) passes the raw JSON text and the manager to the factory, fails fast on empty names or factories, on a T that already has a reader and on duplicate (T, type) pairs, and installs a private GenericCnjTypeReader<T> on first use.
cna_tool_gltf_to_cnj is built unconditionally, links no graphics device or window and is the only CNJ producer; no XNA-to-CNJ exporter exists.
tokens: never initialises a window, a graphics device or a renderer
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 the same conversion is also compiled into cna_content (ConvertGltfToCnj) and used by cna-content and the CNB tools.

concepts.text: ModelTypeReader also reads .gltf/.glb directly through the shared GltfImportCore; the audited runtime path imported only the first mesh group at unit scale 1.0.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 every group is assembled into one Model (SkinsEXT); unit scale is still fixed at 1.0 at run time.

concepts.text: No .cnj file was committed; every CNJ test wrote its fixture at run time, while glTF fixtures were committed.
concepts.note: Inventory snapshot. At 009d40f5 one .cnj is committed (tests/assets/content_pipeline_cmake/Nested/curve.cnj, a pipeline CMake fixture) and CNJ tests still write their documents at run time; no page claim depends on the count.

concepts.text: CNJ Model sidecars are read by hand: .skeleton.bin carries bone count, hierarchy, bind and inverse-bind poses plus an optional appended root-prefix block detected by the remaining byte count, with bone counts capped at 100,000.

ParseXnbHeader reads the 10-byte header (XNB, platform, version, flags, Int32 total length) one magic byte at a time through BinaryReader, a deliberate deviation from FNA so a truncated file throws EndOfStreamException.
Exactly FNA's sixteen platform bytes are accepted (MonoGame's later identifiers are refused, pinned by MonoGameWebAssemblyPlatformIsNotAcceptedMatchingFnaExactly) and the version byte must be 4 or 5.

concepts.text: Compression is a four-valued enum from flag bits 0x80 (LZX) and 0x40 (LZ4); both bits set is Unknown and refused, and both values were confirmed against MonoGame's ContentManager.cs.
tokens: Both bit values were taken from MonoGame's own

concepts.text: LzxDecoder is a line-by-line port of FNA's LzxDecoder.cs with window exponent 15-21 and per-file decoder state; the audited revision refused LZ4 with a named exception.
tokens: LZ4 is one bounded raw block
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 MonoGame's single raw LZ4 block is decoded on the typed path.

concepts.text: DecompressXnbPayload validates compressed and decompressed sizes before allocating, walks the two-byte big-endian block framing with a 0xFF five-byte extended form, and requires the output to equal the declared size.
tokens: a leading 0xFF selects the five-byte form

concepts.text: ParseXnbTypeReaderTable bounds the 7-bit reader count (4,096) and names (1 MiB, after the read), keeps raw and normalised names, and rethrows name-parser errors as ContentLoadException; XnbTypeName parses nested generic names recursively with a depth bound.
tokens: keeps both the raw name and its normalised canonical key

concepts.text: ContentTypeReaderBase is the forced rename of FNA's non-generic ContentTypeReader, ContentTypeReader<T> keeps the XNA name, TargetType is a canonical string, move-only T is boxed as shared_ptr<T> in std::any, and existingInstance is std::optional<T>.

Reader-version enforcement (SupportsVersion defaulting to equality with TypeVersion) is a CNA addition FNA lacks; no built-in overrides it, so an XNB declaring a nonzero version for a built-in reader is rejected.
tokens: FNA reads the integer and ignores it

concepts.text: CanDeserializeIntoExistingObject is declared and overridden to true by ListReader and DictionaryReader but ContentReader never consults it.
concepts.note: Recorded as WP12-i013.

concepts.text: ContentTypeReaderManager is the sole, process-wide registry of reader factories; AddTypeCreator silently keeps the first factory for a key, CreateReader returns a fresh reader per call and ClearTypeCreators exists for test isolation.
tokens: keeps the first factory for an exact key

concepts.text: ContentReader extends BinaryReader as a one-shot session over one file's object graph; its manager pointer may be null, unlike XNA, and ReadAsset<T> initialises the table, reads the root and then the shared resources.
tokens: holds its stream and manager as raw pointers

concepts.text: Object dispatch uses one-based reader indices (0 means null; a null T with no default constructor throws), bounded by an RAII ObjectDepthGuard at 256 that restores the counter on every exit.

Shared resources are two-pass: fixups queue against one-based indices and every shared object is read before any fixup runs, so references may point forward or form cycles; the count is bounded at 1,000,000.
tokens: references may point forward and may form cycles

concepts.text: ReadObject offers FNA's typed forms plus a non-template std::any ReadObject() for untyped Tag fields that does not record disposables.

ReadExternalReference<T> returns std::optional<T>, was explicitly instantiated for Texture2D and TextureCube only, and rejects absolute, drive-letter and UNC references and resolutions above the root while allowing legitimate .. siblings.
tokens: instantiated for Texture2D, TextureCube and shared_ptr<Effect>
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 a third instantiation, shared_ptr<Effect>, serves EffectMaterial references.

concepts.text: LooseFileContentTypeReader<T> is a separate CNA-original interface (Read(path, manager) plus GetExtensions) registered per manager by C++ type, renamed out of ContentTypeReader<T> to free that name for the real XNA class; confusing it with the process-wide XNB registry is the subsystem's most common mistake.
A game type with a reader defined entirely outside CNA loads from .xnb through AddTypeCreator alone; CustomContentTypeReaderTests proves it with a GameLevelData reader and a hand-built XNB.
An XNB compiled with XNA's reflective reader fallback could not be loaded at all; there was no ReflectiveReader.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 ReflectiveTypeReaderBuilder<T> declares the field list once and registers a reader; there is still no automatic reflection.

concepts.text: The general EffectReader was a deliberate KnownUnsupportedContentTypeReader that always threw with a structured reason.
tokens: It accepts no .fx source, HLSL, DXBC or MGFX
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 the real EffectReader constructs Effect(device, bytes) on renderers with compiled-effect support.

concepts.text: XnbReadLimits carries seven limits (file 64 MiB, decompressed 256 MiB, strings 1 MiB, 4,096 readers, 1,000,000 shared resources, 10,000,000 collection elements, nesting 256), each enforced at a named site.
tokens: Limits and where each is enforced

concepts.text: ReadBytesExactOrThrow exists because BinaryReader::ReadBytes silently trims on truncation while callers passed the declared count to pointer APIs, a confirmed heap-buffer-overflow; every declared-length blob read uses it.
CheckedMultiplyOrThrow division-checks each multiplication because widening to int64 was not enough: two near-INT32_MAX dimensions times four overflow int64 itself (found by UBSan).

Texture2DReader checks positive dimensions, checked byte size, the device maximum dimension and a complete-or-level-0 mip chain; the device check was added after the fuzzer produced real process crashes on two GPU renderers, and level byte counts are compared with block-rounded expectations.
tokens: every texture level's byte count against the block-rounded size

concepts.text: Three deterministic fuzz or property harnesses exist: a container mutator loading real fixtures 1,500 times each through ContentManager (std::bad_alloc counts as a failure), an LZX payload fuzzer and a WAVEFORMATEX boundary sweep.

LzxDecoderDifferentialTests compares CNA's LZX output byte for byte with FNA's unmodified decoder run under Mono, a genuine cross-implementation oracle that found a heap overflow in the decode-table growth path.
tokens: A writer and a reader that share one wrong assumption agree with each other

concepts.text: PathContainment.hpp in modules/core provides IsDisallowedAbsolutePath, component-wise ValidateContainedPath (content-evil is not inside content) and ResolveContainedPathRelativeToFile, which confines a file inside the root to the root and an explicitly loaded outside-root file to its own folder.
ContentPathContainmentTests covers traversal, absolute and Unicode-shaped paths and existing-symlink escapes, and asserts rejection before file access without poisoning the cache.

Containment has stated limits: symlink checks are not race-proof, dot segments and .. that normalises inside the root are accepted, and only file-internal references are contained, not the caller's own asset name.
tokens: Symlink checking is not claimed to be race-proof

concepts.text: The CNJ side is less hardened than XNB: no size or depth limit, no fuzzing, and legacy scanners that accept malformed JSON (a truncated SpriteFont document yielded a partial font).
tokens: still reads Model, custom-GLSL Effect and skinned-model fields with substring scanners

concepts.text: The glTF suite is a layered conformance ladder with differential oracles, and GltfKnownDefectTests pins open defects as executable tests with a meta-test keeping the defect ledger and tests in sync.
concepts.note: The ladder has grown to L0-L7 and every ledger record is fixed at 009d40f5.

concepts.text: A fresh ContentManager loads real Texture2D, TextureCube, Model, SpriteFont, SoundEffect and Song fixtures once the built-ins are registered, pinned by XnbBuiltInReaderRegistrationTests.
XnbBuiltInReaderRegistrationTests asserted DecimalReader unconditionally although its registration depends on SHARP_RUNTIME_HAS_NATIVE_INT128.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: at 009d40f5 the assertion is guarded by #if SHARP_RUNTIME_HAS_NATIVE_INT128 and expects the reader absent otherwise (WINCLOSE-0031 comment); also WP12-i017.

concepts.text: Primitive readers (Boolean, Byte, SByte, Int16/32/64, UInt16/32/64, Single, Double, Char, String) are thin BinaryReader delegates reading explicit little-endian fields.
Math readers (vectors, Matrix, Quaternion, Color, Plane, Point, Rectangle, bounding volumes, Ray) delegate to ContentReader helpers in FNA field order; BoundingFrustum reads one Matrix.
BoundingFrustumReader was tested for registration only, with no round-trip value test.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 XnbWriterTest.ABoundingFrustumRoundTripsAsItsMatrix writes and reads a frustum back; the gap claim is not carried over.

concepts.text: Decimal is registered only with a native 128-bit integer, TimeSpan reads Int64 ticks, and DateTime decodes ticks but discards DateTimeKind because System::DateTime cannot store it.
Collection templates follow FNA's existing-instance quirks: ArrayReader resizes, ListReader appends without clearing, DictionaryReader clears first, NullableReader maps to std::optional.

Only three closed collection instantiations (the List<Rectangle>, List<char>, List<Vector3> SpriteFont needs) were registered; each closed generic must be hand-registered because CNA has no reflection.

concepts.note: At 009d40f5 eleven closed combinations are pre-registered; others still need explicit registration.
